title: The journey of the blue glaze
description: Three cards following the blue glaze technique into India in the fourteenth century, to Jaipur in the seventeenth, and under the School of Art from 1866.

u0001.text: The blue glaze travelled into India and reached Jaipur by way of Delhi.

u0004.text: The technique travelled to India with early Muslim rulers and Turkish conquests.

u0007.text: It reached the plains of Delhi and went on to Jaipur.

u0010.text: Blue glaze pottery thrived under the Jaipur School of Art.

u0013.text: The GI application for Blue Pottery of Jaipur was filed on 14 August 2006.

C054.text: The blue glaze technique travelled to India in the 14th century, with early Muslim rulers and Turkish conquests.

quotes.quote: This technique traveled south to India with early Muslim potentates in the 14th century.
The magnificent technique of blue pottery, Turko-Persian in origin, reached East India with Turkish conquests in the 14th century

C057.text: The blue glaze technique grew beyond an architectural accessory to Kashmiri potters, reached the plains of Delhi and went to Jaipur in the 17th century.

quotes.quote: Gradually the blue glaze technique grew beyond an architectural accessory to Kashmiri potters.
From there, the technique traveled to the plains of Delhi
It travelled from Delhi to Jaipur in the 17th century.
it was later introduced in Delhi and moved to Jaipur artisans in the 17th century.

C061.text: Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II set up a school of art at Jaipur in 1866, and blue glaze pottery thrived primarily under its aegis.

quotes.quote: Sawai Ram Singh tr (1835-1880) set up a school of art in 1866
the School of Art was established in 1866 at Jaipur
Introduced in Jaipur from Delhi and Khurja by the ruler of Jaipur, Ram Singh II, blue glaze pottery thrived primarily under the aegis of the Jaipur School of Art, founded in 1866.

C135.text: Blue Pottery of Jaipur was filed for registration as geographical indication application 66 by the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) on 14 August 2006.
